Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before we spin up a sandbox: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: 2–4 week hosted PoC to validate chat-based fraud-detection assistant and lower-latency suggestions for agents.
- Preference: Start on Hosted API for fastest onramp; Dedicated is on the table if throughput/cost targets push in that direction later.
- Data residency: US-only for now.

Open items for your confirmation
1) Traffic profile: rough sustained RPS and expected burst behavior (we need this to size endpoint rate caps).
2) Auth: will you use API key or need SAML/SSO and workspace access?
3) Procurement timeline: when would legal/proc start (helps us provision trial limits and procurement paperwork cadence)?

What we'll do next (proposed)
- I will provision sandbox endpoints and a temporary API key scoped to the PoC (2 sandbox endpoints: chat and completions).
- Share a short quickstart checklist (attached) and a minimal prompt set for quality gating.
- Configure endpoint rate caps for your expected profile (we can iterate).
- Schedule 30m ops sync with your infra lead to confirm network/firewall rules for accessing the sandbox.

Please reply with the three confirmation items above. If estimates are fuzzy, a small range is fine — we just need enough to size initial caps.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Thanks Sean — great demo. A few answers inline and one attachment with our traffic sketch.

- Traffic profile: we expect ~25 RPS sustained during business hours for agent assist. Short bursts to ~100 RPS for <5s on heavy days (end-of-month reconciliation). Total monthly token estimate ~150M tokens.
- Auth: API keys are fine for the PoC. For production we'll need SAML and workspace isolation.
- Procurement: procurement will start once PoC shows latency and quality targets; likely 3–4 weeks after PoC kickoff.

Questions from our side:
- How does Hosted rate limiting behave under burst? Do tokens queue or are requests rejected when caps hit?
- Can we map chat sessions to a single endpoint to preserve KV cache for better latency?
- Any cost recommendations for prompt design to reduce token spend during PoC?

I've attached a simple traffic profile: ivypay-traffic-profile.xlsx

Thanks — can do a quick ops sync Wed if that works for your infra team.

—
Alex Moreno

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Quickstart access patterns & rate caps

Alex — thanks for the details and attachment, that helps. Short answers to your questions and ops notes: 

- Rate limiting behavior: for Hosted we offer two configurable behaviors: a) soft queueing (short in-memory queue with degraded concurrency) or b) immediate 429 rejection when cap exceeded. For PoC we recommend soft queueing + conservative per-call timeout (1.5–2.0s) to avoid silent failures.

- Endpoint mapping & KV cache: yes — we can map the chat flow to a dedicated chat endpoint so the KV cache is preserved for session affinity. That will materially reduce latency on follow-ups. We'll need a session id to be passed with requests.

- Cost recommendations: 1) Prefer system prompts with fewer tokens and move heavy context into embeddings + lookup when possible. 2) Use response length caps for agent suggestions and then fetch expanded content only on demand. 3) We can provide per-call quantization and model-reco that trades off a few % quality for >30% cost savings.

Next steps I propose:
- Sean: provision sandbox keys with these constraints (soft queueing, per-key rate cap 100 RPS burst, 25 RPS sustained).
- Alex: confirm Wednesday availability for 30m ops call (we'll include one of our infra engineers).
- Camila: I will create a short prompt-set and quick eval harness to surface regressions during the PoC.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-ivypay-eval (shared folder with checklist + prompts)

—
